newsitem.title: USA: Democrat denies decision made in Gingrich case.
newsitem.headline: Democrat denies decision made in Gingrich case.

text.p: House Democratic Whip David Bonior Thursday denied a news report that an ethics committee panel had agreed on what punishment to recommend for House Speaker Newt Gingrich for ethics violations.

Bonior, in a statement, accused Republicans of leaking the report in "one more desperate attempt by the Republican leadership to shore up the speaker's crumbling credibility in the light of his own admission that he lied to Congress and lied to the American people."

A news report earlier said the four members of an ethics subcommittee -- two Republicans and two Democrats -- had agreed they would recommend to the full committee that it seek a reprimand of Gingrich.

Under committee rules a reprimand is appropriate for "serious violations" of House ethics rules but is less severe that the penalties of expulsion or censure. It would not require that Gingrich step down as speaker.

The news report Thursday followed distribution earlier this week of a letter by the two Republican members of the subcommittee, Reps. Porter Goss of Florida and Steve Schiff of New Mexico, in which they said they knew of no reason why Gingrich would be ineligible to serve as speaker.

Following a two-year investigation the subcommittee said Dec. 21 that Gingrich had had provided misleading information to investigators and had failed to ensure tax-exempt funds were not used for partisan purposes.
The full ethics committee must recommend a punishment to the full House but will not begin this process until after Gingrich seeks re-election as speaker when Congress convenes Tuesday.
Bonior, a leading Democratic critic of Gingrich, said the news report Thursday "is inaccurate and untrue."
He said he had spoken to members of the ethics committee with an intimate knowledge of the Gingrich case and they had assured him that the news report was wrong.
"I expect members of the committee will soon clarify this mistake," he said.
